body.statement: In the deterministic multitape Turing bit model, can \(\mathsf{FastCert}_n(e,\alpha,\xi)\) be constructed so that, for fixed \(c,K,L_q,L_r,B\), its bit complexity is bounded by a polynomial in \(n\), the total input length \(\Lambda_n\), and \(\xi^{-1}\)? On every feasible input for which \(\mathsf{Cert}_n\) returns \(a_n\), it must terminate with \(\widetilde a_n\) satisfying \(a_n\le\widetilde a_n\le a_n+\xi\) and \(\sup_{q'\in\mathcal Q_n(e),r'\in\mathcal R}\mathbb E H_{\widetilde a_n,h_n}(Z_{r',q'})\le\alpha-\Delta_n\). Can this be achieved with the certified pruning invariant in the branch-and-bound handle while retaining the \(13/32\) late-ramp certificate and the \(0.442M\) high-hazard oracle bound, with only \(\xi\) added to a reported computational radius?
body.justification: The exhaustive certificate establishes computability but may be expensive; a complexity-controlled certificate is the first-class unresolved computational-statistical question.
body.gap: Neither classical compound-Poisson approximation nor selective randomization inference gives a polynomial-time outward-rounded optimization over continuous signed profile classes.
body.consumer: A polynomial certificate would make prespecified daily calibration feasible at the GUSTO-1 and EUROPA trial scales.
